-2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:11404  MFA No. 100382 of 2015  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant/injured seeking enhancement of compensation being aggrieved by judgment and award dated 27.08.2014 passed in MVC No.3007/2012 on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Saundatti1.
2.

entities.text: Senior Civil Judge & Addl. MACT, Saundatti1
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Smt. Shaila Bellikatti, learned counsel for the appellant/injured submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income and disability of the injured and it has awarded meager compensation under each heads.
She further submits that no compensation is awarded under the head of loss of amenities.
It is also submitted that due to head injury, the appellant is unable to carryout routine work.
Hence, she seeks to re-assess the entire compensation appropriately by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. S.S. Koliwad for respondent No.2 and Sri.S.S. Joshi, learned counsel for respondent No.4 in chorus oppose the appeal and submit that taking note of the nature of injuries sustained by the injured, 'Tribunal' for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11404 the Tribunal has assessed disability of the injured at 30% to the whole body, which is on the higher side.
They submit that the award of compensation by the Tribunal on all other heads is just and proper and does not call for enhancement.
Thus, they seek dismissal of appeal.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including original records of the Tribunal.

5. The material available on record indicates that on 16.5.2012, the appellant was proceeding on Tata Truck bearing registration No.KA-30/2544, as a cleaner, from Naragund to Blegaum, at that time, he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately, he was shifted to Dr. R.B.
Patagundi Hospital, Gokak, wherein he took treatment as inpatient for three days and later he was taken to Lakeview Hospital, Belgaum, where he was an inpatient for about one month.
In support of the claim, the injured himself examined as PW1 and examined one doctor as PW2, who deposed that the appellant has sustained 30% disability to the whole body due to accidental injuries.

This Court taking note that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:11404 appellant has suffered three fractures in the skull and three hemorrhagic contusions in the skull, is of the opinion that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability of the injured at 37% to the whole body.

Admittedly, the appellant has not Hanamant Fakirappa Sogalad vs Riyazahammed Naxirahmed Pathan on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199158244/
2 produced any evidence with regard to income.

sentences.text: The pleadings and evidence on record indicate that the appellant was working as cleaner-cum-driver in the lorry.
However, no cogent and acceptable evidence with regard to income of the appellant is placed on record.
This Court placing reliance on notional income chart prepared by KSLSA, would re-
assess the notional income of the appellant at Rs.6,500/- per month.

Thus, loss of future earnings due to disability would be Rs.5,19,480/-
(Rs.6,500 x 12 x 18 x 37/100).
6.

Taking note of the fact that appellant has sustained three fractures and also took treatment for about more than one month, the compensation is reassessed as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 60,000/-

Medical expenses Rs.1,65,976/-
Food, diet, nourishment, attendant & transportation charges Rs. 45,000/-
Loss of income during laid-up period Rs. 27,000/- Loss of future earnings due to disability Rs.5,19,480/-

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands partly allowed.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.8,67,456/- as against Rs.5,76,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
d) The respondent No.2/Insurer shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
